_comment: Curated appliance/device-class -> expected primary telemetry category
for the Phase A10 'unmonitored-capability check' (the Infoblox
problem): a device whose main security value depends on a specific
log stream can sit in a customer's Assets or Security Tooling sheet
with that stream never declared in Log Sources -- silently useless
for detection. expected_category values are the SAME coarse telemetry
categories ranking.py's log-source/tooling bridge already uses
(endpoint/registry/network/identity/cloud/application/mobile/ot) --
enforced by test_mitre_quality.py against the real bridge category
set, never a fourth taxonomy. keywords match the SAME substring-over-
normalized-text discipline as ranking.py's _categories_provided (no
new normalizer). Seed set is deliberately small (precision over
recall, same discipline as keyword_aliases.json) -- 8 classes chosen
from real customer environment-workbook patterns seen in Acme-class
testing (2026-08-03) plus common appliance categories every mid-size
org's inventory tends to include.
telemetry_label is the plain-English log type used in both 'no X is
declared' and 'declaring/enabling X would...' sentence slots (see
quality.unmonitored_capability_check); capability is the one-line
plain-English reason the device's logs matter for detection.

classes.label: EDR platform
classes.capability: catching malicious activity on your endpoints

classes.capability: logging and blocking malicious network traffic
